## DD-B — the fresh-eyes campaign (October 14, 2026; Pre-Deploy S13; 62 rows DDB-1 … DDB-62, every one homed to the new row S13b "DD-B fixes", the three P1s first; its nine design rows RULED the same day (`DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md` §DD-B), their builds DDB-R1 … R7, the siblings found while ruling DDB-X1 … X4, and two rows brought in from the post-deploy backlog, DDB-X5 … X6, in the second table; **S13b part 1 LANDED October 14, 2026**: DDB-1 … DDB-12 and DDB-X5 FIXED (`08c54539`, `6f360d03`), with the siblings its sweeps found, DDB-X7 … X11 — X7, X8 and X10 FIXED in the part, X9 and X11 head part 2; **S13b part 2 LANDED October 15, 2026**: DDB-X9, DDB-X11, DDB-13 … 20 and DDB-22 … 44 FIXED (`8f3f1141`, `33643c45`, `cd8f3210`), with the siblings its sweeps found, DDB-X12 … X22 — all FIXED in the part but DDB-X17, which heads part 3; **S13b part 3 LANDED October 15, 2026**: DDB-X17 FIXED, DDB-R1 … R7 BUILT and DDB-X1 … X3 FIXED (`eba57ba4`, `ab6314a9`, `89db8acc`), with the siblings its sweeps found, DDB-X23 … X25 — all FIXED in the part; **S13b part 4 LANDED October 19, 2026**: DDB-21, DDB-45 … 62 and DDB-X6 FIXED (`94ce4c44`, the close), with the siblings its sweeps found, DDB-X26 … X32 — all FIXED in the part; **S13b COMPLETE: 0 rows homed to S13b OPEN** (DDB-X4 heads S14 with SFR-B3 — **FIXED in S14 part 4, October 20, 2026**; DD-B's re-measure is S14e))

> Three players who had read nothing played 20 turns each IN THE CLIENT at 5120×1440 (Interface Scale 1.4, a first launch), one road each — conquest, diplomacy-first, the sea — through `tools/dd_b_client.gd` / `tools/dd_b_play.py` against a sandboxed backend (never 8005), and filed every confusion with its frame. Every typed line was read by the ONE judge (`tools/_score_probes.py`; it learned two reply shapes, each checked against every committed census record first); it reads **0 P1**. The write-up is `docs/audits/DD_B_FRESH_EYES_2026_10_14.md`; the records `docs/audits/dd_b/` (`causes.json`, `metric.json`, and per road `rows.json`, `judge.json`, `actions.log`, `summaries.md`, the cited frames); rules `SYSTEMS_REFERENCE.md` §115.
>
> **How these rows were filed.** 96 player rows (34 + 34 + 28) were read against the code (each row's cause is traced to file:line) and de-duplicated across the three roads: one cause sighted several times is one row naming every sighting and its frame. One conquest row was struck as an instrument artifact (the summary cut the opening dispatch's first marshal line; the game lists Massena). A row's severity is the worst of its sightings, as the players graded them. **The metric** (`metric.json`): 69 causes in 60 turns = **11.5 rows per 10 turns** (P1 0.5 · P2 3.5 · P3 7.5); per road conquest 14.0, diplomacy-first 16.0, the sea 12.5. **Done-when (under 5 per 10 turns and 0 P1): NOT met** — so every row is filed and homed to S13b, P1s first. Nothing was fixed in S13.
>
> **The rulings (October 14, 2026, after the close, under the user's delegation: "make design calls please do research and assure the plan has all errors fixed in coming sessions and any similar errors they find while working").** DDB-D1 … D9 are RULED (`docs/audits/DD_B_RULINGS_2026_10_14.md`). D8 and D9's mechanics ride the P1 rows DDB-2 and DDB-3; the other seven builds are DDB-R1 … R7. Four siblings were found while ruling (DDB-X1 … X4). The same day the user brought two items forward from the post-deploy backlog ("i agree"): DW-2, the bilateral scorer's victory weight (DDB-X5), and the naval rail alerts (DDB-X6).
>
> **S13b's parts** (`PRE_DEPLOY_PLAN.md` §2): part 1 the P1s with D8 / D9 built, then the table's P2s (DDB-1 … 12, X5) · part 2 the table's P3s and the field (DDB-13 … 20, 22 … 44) · part 3 the rulings and their siblings (DDB-R1 … R7, X1 … X3) · part 4 the voice, the client and the sea (DDB-21, 45 … 62, X6). DDB-X4 lands with SFR-B3 at S14's head. **The re-measure** (three fresh players, the same brief and roads) moved on October 14, 2026 to **S14e**, after the new features (VP-1, events, the table lesson), so it reads the game Round 0 will meet; its new rows are filed by DD-B's rule, and if the done-when is not met they become **S14f** before S15.
>
> **The sibling sweep (from S13b on, the user's ruling):** every fix ends with a search for its class — the same mechanism on the other courts, dialogues, popups and roads, and the AI's side of the same executor. Each sibling found is filed here as a found row (DDB-X…, tagged) and fixed in the same slice with its own test; one too large for the slice heads the next part. Nothing found is homed after the deploy.

| **DDB-19** | P2 | FIXED October 15, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 2 (`cd8f3210`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_field.py::TestDDB19`; `objection_v2.muster_expected_totals` — the attack objection (`_get_attack_odds_ratio`, `personality._get_strength_ratio`) reads the muster's committed totals at FULL / PARTIAL; pure (the hint latch put back); the sighting's re-play is DD-B's re-measure, S14e, which reads every road again); was: the decided fix below holds, `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_field.py::TestDDB19` pins it, and S13b's closing re-play on the DD-B instrument shows the sighting gone ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=marshal_drama⟩ | **An objection's odds and the muster's band disagree on the same attack.** The attack objection reads the marshal's own corps against one enemy marshal (`personality.py:295-305`, `:388-411`; `disobedience.py:605-607`); the muster counts every corps in reach (102k vs 52k). **Sightings:** diplomacy-first #9 (P2, turn 2, action 64, `docs/audits/dd_b/diplomacy/frames/0064.jpg`). **Decided fix:** The attack objection reads the muster's expected totals. |
| **DDB-20** | P2 | FIXED October 15, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 2 (`cd8f3210`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_field.py::TestDDB20`; `strategic.support_stands_at_approach`: a SUPPORT whose next step is the ally's contested field stands at the approach, order standing, at the order's issue and at the turn's tick; SUPPORT on the same field is exempt from the engagement gate; the sighting's re-play is DD-B's re-measure, S14e, which reads every road again); was: the decided fix below holds, `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_field.py::TestDDB20` pins it, and S13b's closing re-play on the DD-B instrument shows the sighting gone ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=combat_legibility⟩ | **The muster's "order him to support" cannot be carried out.** A literal marshal's SUPPORT whose first step meets the enemy in the supported man's contested province hits the "reached the approach" branch, which clears the order and charges 1 AP (`strategic_executor.py:2630-2660`), so the next muster again reads him as "awaits explicit orders"; and a marshal on the battle's own field is engaged, so the strategic gate refuses his SUPPORT outright (`strategic_executor.py:813-841`) while the muster advises it (`display_names.py:808-810`). **Sightings:** diplomacy-first #11 (P2, turn 2, action 75, `docs/audits/dd_b/diplomacy/frames/0075.jpg`); diplomacy-first #14 (P3, turn 3, action 94, `docs/audits/dd_b/diplomacy/frames/0094.jpg`). **Decided fix:** A SUPPORT whose destination is the supported marshal's contested province stays standing and joins his next attack as a reinforcement; SUPPORT of a marshal in the same province is exempt from the engagement gate. |
| **DDB-21** | P2 | FIXED October 19, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 4 (`94ce4c44`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_sea.py::TestDDB21`; a corps on soil its court holds by title is home — `withdrawal.is_home_at` / `game_end.holds_by_title`, read by the stranded predicate, the tick's arrival, the AI's next step and the dispatch; the corridor opened AFTER the status quo's titles; ONE embark rule, `naval.embark_position_ok` (the home zone walked by land): a corps on our own shore across the water embarks; measured before: Lannes on titled Munster warned three times and interned on the fourth tick; the siblings DDB-X26, X27; the CMD-H-DOWN driven arm re-seated with the title seam named (Wellesley on titled Andalusia fortifies instead of walking home); the sighting's re-play is DD-B's re-measure, S14e, which reads every road again); was: the decided fix below holds, `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_sea.py::TestDDB21` pins it, and S13b's closing re-play on the DD-B instrument shows the sighting gone ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=naval⟩ | **A corps standing in a province the peace just titled to France is "stranded" and faces internment.** The home zone is a land path from Paris (`withdrawal.py:354-392`, `:445-461`), so Oudinot in Munster (French by the treaty) is stranded and must walk home through Britain in two turns, while the embark rule treats the same ground as home soil that needs a dockyard (`naval_executor.py:402-406`). **Sightings:** the sea #21 (P2, turn 11, action 302, `docs/audits/dd_b/sea/frames/0302.jpg`). **Decided fix:** A corps on a province France holds by title is home; a corps outside the home zone may embark from its own coastal province. |
| **DDB-22** | P3 | FIXED October 15, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 2 (`33643c45`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_table.py::TestDDB22`; the harsher per-court dial reads "Demand more of <court>"; the sighting's re-play is DD-B's re-measure, S14e, which reads every road again); was: the decided fix below holds, `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_table.py::TestDDB22` pins it, and S13b's closing re-play on the DD-B instrument shows the sighting gone ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=diplomacy⟩ | **"Press <court>" means a separate peace in the advice and harsher terms on the button.** `settlement_staging.py:2455` ("Press {court} alone: the separate peace") against the per-court button "Press {court}" = `settlement_dial_harsher` (`:3375-3382`). **Sightings:** conquest #11 (P3, turn 4, action 87, `docs/audits/dd_b/conquest/frames/0087.jpg`). **Decided fix:** The button reads "Demand more of <court>". |
| **DDB-23** | P3 | FIXED October 15, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 2 (`33643c45`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_table.py::TestDDB23`; `display_names.stream_term_phrase` names every stream's term ("for as long as the treaty stands", or its turns); the treaty itself stands first; the sighting's re-play is DD-B's re-measure, S14e, which reads every road again); was: the decided fix below holds, `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_table.py::TestDDB23` pins it, and S13b's closing re-play on the DD-B instrument shows the sighting gone ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=diplomacy⟩ | **A per-turn payment or action is offered with no duration.** "More generous" adds `gold_per_turn` (or, a round later, `ap_per_turn`) with no `turns` — bilateral streams are perpetual by design — and the display template has no duration slot (`diplomatic_templates.py:4504-4517`, `:4736-4740`; `diplomatic_executor.py:5320-5337`); on an armistice it replaces the armistice line in the term list. **Sightings:** conquest #31 (P3, turn 18, action 345, `docs/audits/dd_b/conquest/frames/0345.jpg`); diplomacy-first #10 (P3, turn 2, action 70, `docs/audits/dd_b/diplomacy/frames/0070.jpg`); diplomacy-first #20 (P3, turn 5, action 151, `docs/audits/dd_b/diplomacy/frames/0151.jpg`). **Decided fix:** Every stream's line names its term ("for as long as the treaty stands", or its turns); a generous round on an armistice keeps the armistice as the first listed term. |
| **DDB-24** | P3 | FIXED October 15, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 2 (`33643c45`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_table.py::TestDDB24`; `settlement_presentation.side_court_label` names the sides by court ("France" / "The Third Coalition"); a court's white peace says it settles the whole war and names the per-court road; the sighting's re-play is DD-B's re-measure, S14e, which reads every road again); was: the decided fix below holds, `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_table.py::TestDDB24` pins it, and S13b's closing re-play on the DD-B instrument shows the sighting gone ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=diplomacy⟩ | **The war's sides read France as attacker while every war purpose reads "Defense".** France is the attacker of record in `starting_wars` (`europe_1805.json:66-73`), so the war instance lists France as Attackers / war leader, while the boot gives every belligerent a defense purpose (`world_state.py:10259-10275`); a white peace from a court's page stages the whole-war settlement on purpose (`diplomatic_executor.py:3505-3515`). **Sightings:** diplomacy-first #2 (P3, turn 1, action 6, `docs/audits/dd_b/diplomacy/frames/0006.jpg`). **Decided fix:** The sides are labelled by court ("France" / "The Third Coalition"), never attacker/defender; the white peace from a court's page says it settles the whole war, beside the per-court road. |
| **DDB-25** | P3 | FIXED October 15, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 2 (`33643c45`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_table.py::TestDDB25`; `assess_terms` opens the feasibility card on Talleyrand's suggested terms with their acceptance ("Propose these terms"); the strength line says who outmatches whom; the sighting's re-play is DD-B's re-measure, S14e, which reads every road again); was: the decided fix below holds, `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_table.py::TestDDB25` pins it, and S13b's closing re-play on the DD-B instrument shows the sighting gone ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=diplomacy⟩ | **"What terms would they accept?" answers with no terms.** The button runs `expand_to_proposal` with no proposal type and lands on the generic standstill menu: no terms, no acceptance (`diplomatic_advisory.py:1296-1301`, `:1953-1962`; `diplomatic_executor.py:5980-6007`); "overmatched" is the bottom of the strength ladder inside "Their military strength is {X} relative to ours" (`diplomatic_templates.py:741-765`). **Sightings:** diplomacy-first #4 (P3, turn 1, action 12, `docs/audits/dd_b/diplomacy/frames/0012.jpg`). **Decided fix:** The button opens the feasibility card (the suggested terms with their acceptance); the strength line reads "we outmatch them" / "they outmatch us". |
| **DDB-26** | P3 | FIXED October 15, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 2 (`33643c45`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_table.py::TestDDB26`; the band promises a counter only when the generator's dry run builds one (`counter_aware_likelihood`); the preview is titled by its treaty, the treaty first, the armistice's mechanics above the score; the sighting's re-play is DD-B's re-measure, S14e, which reads every road again); was: the decided fix below holds, `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_table.py::TestDDB26` pins it, and S13b's closing re-play on the DD-B instrument shows the sighting gone ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=diplomacy⟩ | **The armistice preview's title, band word and term list disagree with the court's page.** The page word is a score band ("Doubtful — may counter", `diplomacy.py:12096-12097`) while the preview runs the real counter generator ("no workable counter", `:4927-4970`); any war-state preview is titled "PEACE PREVIEW" and lists only clauses, never the treaty itself (`proposal_confirm_popup.gd:186-187`); the armistice's mechanics block renders last (`:1477-1490`). **Sightings:** diplomacy-first #10 (P3, turn 2, action 70, `docs/audits/dd_b/diplomacy/frames/0070.jpg`). **Decided fix:** The preview is titled by its treaty type and lists the treaty as its first term; the band word drops "may counter" unless a counter is constructible; the mechanics block stands above the score. |
| **DDB-27** | P3 | FIXED October 15, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 2 (`33643c45`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_table.py::TestDDB27`; the assessment reads the war score live (`live_war_score_for`); the battlefield line only while a victory is wanting; the sighting's re-play is DD-B's re-measure, S14e, which reads every road again); was: the decided fix below holds, `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_table.py::TestDDB27` pins it, and S13b's closing re-play on the DD-B instrument shows the sighting gone ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=diplomacy⟩ | **Talleyrand's assessment ignores the battles fought since the last end turn.** `get_assessment_text` reads the stored `war_scores`, recalculated only at end turn (`diplomacy.py:12166-12173`, `:3820-3835`); battles only append records (`:10393-10405`), while the war panel computes the score live (`war_status.py:153-157`); `:13738` is the unconditional fallback line. **Sightings:** diplomacy-first #12 (P3, turn 2, action 80, `docs/audits/dd_b/diplomacy/frames/0080.jpg`). **Decided fix:** The assessment reads `calculate_war_score` live; the fallback line is gated on the score. |
| **DDB-28** | P3 | FIXED October 15, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 2 (`33643c45`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_table.py::TestDDB28`; the review's petition line carries Grant / Decline (`settlement_answer_petition` → `answer_ally_petition_from_table`) on the staged draft; the sighting's re-play is DD-B's re-measure, S14e, which reads every road again); was: the decided fix below holds, `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_table.py::TestDDB28` pins it, and S13b's closing re-play on the DD-B instrument shows the sighting gone ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=vassals⟩ | **An ally's petition over the settlement arrives only after the settlement is ratified.** Staging the settlement queues the ally's petition behind the settlement dialogue; the review shows it as a line with no control (`proposal_confirm_popup.gd:582-594`); it becomes current only after ratification, when the draft is gone, so Grant is refused ("The draft has moved on", `settlement_offers.py:1686-1687`, `settlement_staging.py:4125-4140`). **Sightings:** diplomacy-first #17 (P3, turn 4, action 131, `docs/audits/dd_b/diplomacy/frames/0131.jpg`). **Decided fix:** The review's petition line carries Grant / Decline acting on the staged draft. |
| **DDB-29** | P3 | FIXED October 15, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 2 (`33643c45`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_table.py::TestDDB29`; `settlement_staging.purge_drafts_naming` at `set_diplomatic_state`: a court that leaves the war leaves no draft naming it; the sighting's re-play is DD-B's re-measure, S14e, which reads every road again); was: the decided fix below holds, `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_table.py::TestDDB29` pins it, and S13b's closing re-play on the DD-B instrument shows the sighting gone ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=diplomacy⟩ | **A ratified separate peace is followed by "your unratified draft … was set aside".** Ratification discards only the draft under its own scope key; the earlier whole-war draft naming the same court survives and is set aside at turn end with its court's name (`world_state.py:11235-11287`, `settlement_ratify.py:1701`, `settlement_staging.py:2617-2634`). **Sightings:** diplomacy-first #18 (P3, turn 5, action 133, `docs/audits/dd_b/diplomacy/frames/0133.jpg`). **Decided fix:** Ratification purges every scoped draft naming a court that just left the war. |
| **DDB-30** | P3 | FIXED October 15, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 2 (`33643c45`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_table.py::TestDDB30`; "Less generous" restores exactly the previous round (`context["previous_round"]`), absent on round 1; the sighting's re-play is DD-B's re-measure, S14e, which reads every road again); was: the decided fix below holds, `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_table.py::TestDDB30` pins it, and S13b's closing re-play on the DD-B instrument shows the sighting gone ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=diplomacy⟩ | **A generous round cannot be stepped back.** The rebuilt options after "More generous" are Send / Even more generous / Not Now (`diplomatic_executor.py:5395-5410`): no way back to the previous round's terms. **Sightings:** diplomacy-first #20 (P3, turn 5, action 151, `docs/audits/dd_b/diplomacy/frames/0151.jpg`). **Decided fix:** A "Less generous" option carries the previous round's terms. |
| **DDB-31** | P3 | FIXED October 15, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 2 (`33643c45`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_table.py::TestDDB31`; the buy-off chip names the design that wakes next and its price (`instruments.next_design_after_buyoff`, a counterfactual put back exactly); the sighting's re-play is DD-B's re-measure, S14e, which reads every road again); was: the decided fix below holds, `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_table.py::TestDDB31` pins it, and S13b's closing re-play on the DD-B instrument shows the sighting gone ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=agendas⟩ | **A bought-off design is followed at once by the next one, unannounced.** The buy-off chip names only the design it buys; `congress._buy_off_chain` (`congress.py:1515-1543`) knows the court's next design and its price (`diplomacy.py:13128-13135`) but the chip never says so. **Sightings:** diplomacy-first #27 (P3, turn 10, action 229, `docs/audits/dd_b/diplomacy/frames/0229.jpg`). **Decided fix:** The buy-off chip names the design that wakes next and its price. |
| **DDB-32** | P3 | FIXED October 15, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 2 (`33643c45`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_table.py::TestDDB32`; the Treaties book lists the 1805 alliances: "an alliance of 1805, not a treaty of ours"; the sighting's re-play is DD-B's re-measure, S14e, which reads every road again); was: the decided fix below holds, `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_table.py::TestDDB32` pins it, and S13b's closing re-play on the DD-B instrument shows the sighting gone ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=diplomacy⟩ | **The ledger's Treaties book reads "No active treaties" while the Cabinet counts the 1805 alliances.** The TREATIES tab lists only `world.active_treaties` records (`diplomatic_ledger.py:890-894`, `diplomatic_ledger.gd:648-663`); the Cabinet's "Treaties (N)" is built from the diplomatic states, where ALLIANCE counts (`main.py:6979-7027`); the 1805 alliances (Spain, Bavaria) carry no treaty record. **Sightings:** the sea #3 (P3, turn 1, action 17, `docs/audits/dd_b/sea/frames/0017.jpg`). **Decided fix:** The Treaties book lists the record-less 1805 alliances with the line "an alliance of 1805, not a treaty of ours". |
| **DDB-33** | P3 | FIXED October 15, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 2 (`33643c45`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_table.py::TestDDB33`; Ease stops at the scorer's gold ceiling (1,000) and says so; the promised-region check counts a client state's provinces; the sighting's re-play is DD-B's re-measure, S14e, which reads every road again); was: the decided fix below holds, `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_table.py::TestDDB33` pins it, and S13b's closing re-play on the DD-B instrument shows the sighting gone ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=diplomacy⟩ | **Easing past 1,000 gold buys nothing, and then offers a province already promised to a new client.** Ease raises gold toward a 1,500 cap while the scorer stops crediting gold at 1,000 (`settlement_staging.py:1352-1356` vs `settlement_scoring.py:545-546`, `:1472-1474`); at the cap the dial offers France-held land, and its promised-region check counts only cede clauses, not the provinces of the "Erect Ireland" clause (`settlement_baseline.py:240-255`), so the validator refuses the draft (`carve_region_double_promised`, `settlement_validation.py:1312-1337`). **Sightings:** the sea #17 (P3, turn 8, action 235, `docs/audits/dd_b/sea/frames/0235.jpg`). **Decided fix:** Ease stops raising gold where the scorer stops counting it, and says so; the promised-region check counts a client state's provinces. |
| **DDB-34** | P3 | FIXED October 15, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 2 (`33643c45`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_table.py::TestDDB34`; the dispatch names "F1 → <court> → Bid for Their Allegiance"; the advice menu offers the bid while an auction is open; the sighting's re-play is DD-B's re-measure, S14e, which reads every road again); was: the decided fix below holds, `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_table.py::TestDDB34` pins it, and S13b's closing re-play on the DD-B instrument shows the sighting gone ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=ai_aliveness⟩ | **The dispatch announces an allegiance auction for three turns and never says where to bid.** The dispatch line names no control (`dispatch.py:6880-6883`); Talleyrand's "What should we do about …" is a fixed peace-time template with no bid (`diplomatic_templates.py:770-796`); the Cabinet's page does carry "Bid for Their Allegiance" (`diplomacy.py:12924`, `:12976-13006`). **Sightings:** the sea #22 (P3, turn 12, action 308, `docs/audits/dd_b/sea/frames/0308.jpg`). **Decided fix:** The dispatch line names the Cabinet chip; the advice menu offers the bid while an auction is open. |
| **DDB-35** | P3 | FIXED October 15, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 2 (`33643c45`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_table.py::TestDDB35`; Propose Peace stands in the WAR state behind the ONE verdict's paradox; the one-on-one refusal names the court's own controls; the sighting's re-play is DD-B's re-measure, S14e, which reads every road again); was: the decided fix below holds, `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_table.py::TestDDB35` pins it, and S13b's closing re-play on the DD-B instrument shows the sighting gone ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=diplomacy⟩ | **A one-on-one war is told to "use bilateral peace", and the court's page offers none.** In the WAR state the Cabinet offers only Propose Armistice; Propose Peace exists only in ARMISTICE (`diplomacy.py:12649-12772`), while the refusal (`display_names.py:954`) and the war panel's "Negotiate Peace" point to it (`war_detail_popup.gd:652-661`); the game can stage a peace straight from war (`settlement_actions.py:3202-3212`). **Sightings:** the sea #24 (P3, turn 14, action 330, `docs/audits/dd_b/sea/frames/0330.jpg`). **Decided fix:** Propose Peace stands in the WAR state, with the ally-at-war hard stop already used in ARMISTICE. |
| **DDB-36** | P3 | FIXED October 15, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 2 (`cd8f3210`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_field.py::TestDDB36`; the header reads "The band weighs more than the men" only when the folded band reads worse than the raw numbers' band, else "Standing modifiers, already in the band"; the cautious line gives "his own 26k against 60k"; the sighting's re-play is DD-B's re-measure, S14e, which reads every road again); was: the decided fix below holds, `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_field.py::TestDDB36` pins it, and S13b's closing re-play on the DD-B instrument shows the sighting gone ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=combat_legibility⟩ | **The muster's posture note reads against its own favourable band.** `_posture_note` opens with "The band weighs more than the men" whenever any modifier hurts, even when the band reads favourable; the cautious −10% is priced on the marshal's SOLO ratio, deliberately (PT-D1) (`combat_executor.py:1889-1912`). **Sightings:** conquest #3 (P3, turn 1, action 14, `docs/audits/dd_b/conquest/frames/0014.jpg`). **Decided fix:** The header prints only when the band is worse than the raw numbers' band; the cautious line gives the solo figures ("his own 26k against 34k"). |
| **DDB-37** | P3 | FIXED October 15, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 2 (`cd8f3210`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_field.py::TestDDB37`; the battle event carries `advanced_to` and the enemy phase says "— and advances into X"; `_BY_RULE_NO_SHOWS` (literal_personality, neutral_soil) skip the "Where was" bank; the sighting's re-play is DD-B's re-measure, S14e, which reads every road again); was: the decided fix below holds, `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_field.py::TestDDB37` pins it, and S13b's closing re-play on the DD-B instrument shows the sighting gone ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=combat_legibility⟩ | **The enemy phase never says a winner advanced, and asks "Where was Soult?" of a corps obeying its order.** A winning AI attacker's advance exists only in the prose message; the dialog builds its lines from structured fields and the battle event has no advance field (`enemy_phase_dialog.gd:198-205`, `:337-346`; `combat_executor.py:9260-9276`); a literal marshal with no SUPPORT order is recorded as a failed reinforcement and the failure bank prints "Where was Soult?" (`combat_executor.py:2980-3009`, `battle_report.py:923-965`). **Sightings:** conquest #4 (P3, turn 2, action 25, `docs/audits/dd_b/conquest/frames/0025.jpg`). **Decided fix:** The battle event carries `advanced_to` and the line says "and advances into Franconia"; the "Where was" bank skips by-rule no-shows. |
| **DDB-38** | P3 | FIXED October 15, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 2 (`cd8f3210`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_field.py::TestDDB38`; `forced_retreat_clears_counter_punch` at every forced retreat (its rail row dismissed); `derive_register` reads a stalemate's field (routed / province lost = defeat; enemy routed / province taken = triumph); the sighting's re-play is DD-B's re-measure, S14e, which reads every road again); was: the decided fix below holds, `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_field.py::TestDDB38` pins it, and S13b's closing re-play on the DD-B instrument shows the sighting gone ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=combat_legibility⟩ | **A "stalemate" can rout the defender: the free-attack card and the "bloody stalemate" banner then lie.** The morale rout is gated only on "not victor" (`combat_executor.py:8360-8364`), so a stalemate can force the defender out, and the attacker then pursues into the emptied province (`:9194-9204`); a cautious defender earns the counter-punch on a stalemate (`combat.py:878-882`) and the normal forced-retreat branch never clears it (`:5512-5551`); the diorama's register reads only the outcome string (`battle_diorama.py:302-320`). **Sightings:** conquest #6 (P3, turn 2, action 35, `docs/audits/dd_b/conquest/frames/0035.jpg`); conquest #28 (P3, turn 17, action 316, `docs/audits/dd_b/conquest/frames/0316.jpg`). **Decided fix:** A forced retreat clears the counter-punch; the diorama's register reads the field (routed / province lost = defeat; enemy routed / province taken = triumph). |

| **DDB-41** | P3 | FIXED October 15, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 2 (`cd8f3210`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_field.py::TestDDB41`; "Cancel the Order (no cost)" on the objection dialog; `cancel` / `withdraw` clear a tactical or strategic objection with no trust, action or authority spent (`objection_withdrawn` on the response); the sighting's re-play is DD-B's re-measure, S14e, which reads every road again); was: the decided fix below holds, `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_field.py::TestDDB41` pins it, and S13b's closing re-play on the DD-B instrument shows the sighting gone ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=ui_ux⟩ | **An objection offers no plain cancel: every answer spends trust or an order.** The objection dialog carries three answers — Proceed as Ordered, Trust <marshal>'s Judgment, Compromise — each priced in trust or AP, and no way to withdraw the order (`objection_dialog.gd:178-196`, `:330-340`). **Sightings:** conquest #23 (P3, turn 14, action 265, `docs/audits/dd_b/conquest/frames/0265.jpg`). **Decided fix:** A Cancel answer withdraws the order at no cost. |

The series arms B and G byte-identical (B reached Austria's two own-soil wins); the sighting's re-play is DD-B's re-measure, S14e, which reads every road again); was: the decided fix below holds, `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_field.py::TestDDB42` pins it, and S13b's closing re-play on the DD-B instrument shows the sighting gone ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=living_balance⟩ | **Europe's alarm rises when France fights on, or retakes, its own soil.** A capture adds +2 threat for any province the capturer did not hold at the START of the campaign, so provinces titled to France by treaty count as conquest every time they are retaken (`world_state.py:4823-4833`); any attacker win adds +3 `battle_win` (`combat_executor.py:4242-4243`), the rule EB-4.3 ("Europe fears the conqueror, not the defender") applied only to the defender role (`:4276-4285`), so driving an invader out of a French homeland province alarms Europe. **Sightings:** conquest #24 (P3, turn 14, action 269, `docs/audits/dd_b/conquest/frames/0269.jpg`); diplomacy-first #26 (P3, turn 8, action 202, `docs/audits/dd_b/diplomacy/frames/0202.jpg`). **Decided fix:** A capture of a province France holds title to, and a win in a province France owns, add no threat; the result line names any threat it does add and why. |
| **DDB-43** | P3 | FIXED October 15, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 2 (`cd8f3210`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_field.py::TestDDB43`; Traced on the record (the conquest run kept no save — a live client session): a province changes controller between two other courts by a capture (`capture_region`, the enemy phase — the record shows Prussia's corps taking provinces in the Fourth Coalition's war while France's corps stood in Franconia), by the reckless auto-charge's mirrored conquest, or by a treaty cession; only an ask-back return (`province_returned`) was ever announced. `announce_third_party_capture` queues "X passes from A to B" and, for our corps standing there when its entry is closed, "Bernadotte stands on Franconia, now Prussia's soil — we are at peace and hold no open borders: he may march out, but no corps of ours may enter it again"; the sighting's re-play is DD-B's re-measure, S14e, which reads every road again); was: the decided fix below holds, `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_field.py::TestDDB43` pins it, and S13b's closing re-play on the DD-B instrument shows the sighting gone ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=living_balance⟩ | **A province passing between other courts goes unannounced, and corps on soil that closed are not told.** Partly traced: entry under ARMISTICE is refused by the movement law (`movement_executor.py:453-486`, `diplomacy.py:10454-10480`); the corps had retreated into Franconia while it was Bavaria's; how it passed to Prussia was not traced, and no dispatch line or map cue marked the change. **Sightings:** conquest #30 (P3, turn 18, action 338, `docs/audits/dd_b/conquest/frames/0338.jpg`). **Decided fix:** Traced first (S13b's own probe on the conquest save); then a province changing hands between other courts is a dispatch line, and corps standing on soil whose entry just closed are told so. |
| **DDB-44** | P3 | FIXED October 15, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 2 (`cd8f3210`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_field.py::TestDDB44`; `movement_executor.supply_warning_line` (the turn's own bill, `WorldState.supply_forecast`) on a move, a march's first step and its turn reports; the sighting's re-play is DD-B's re-measure, S14e, which reads every road again); was: the decided fix below holds, `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_field.py::TestDDB44` pins it, and S13b's closing re-play on the DD-B instrument shows the sighting gone ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=economy⟩ | **A march into a crowded province gives no supply warning; the shortage strikes at turn start.** Supply attrition is charged at the turn's tick (`world_state.py:7888-7951`); its forecast exists only in the battle muster (`combat_executor.py:2408-2454`), never on a move. **Sightings:** diplomacy-first #7 (P3, turn 2, action 49, `docs/audits/dd_b/diplomacy/frames/0049.jpg`). **Decided fix:** A move or march into a province whose supply the stack outruns says so in its reply, with the forecast loss. |
| **DDB-45** | P3 | FIXED October 19, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 4 (`94ce4c44`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_voice.py::TestDDB45`; the compound question (`question_desk.classify_compound_question`), each part answered on its line; `enemy_at` places a foe only after "at / in" (`state_desk._place_after_foe`); the siblings DDB-X28, X29; the sighting's re-play is DD-B's re-measure, S14e, which reads every road again); was: the decided fix below holds, `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_voice.py::TestDDB45` pins it, and S13b's closing re-play on the DD-B instrument shows the sighting gone ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=command⟩ | **A two-part question is read as one, and answered wrong or not at all.** Every classifier reads a line as ONE question: in "how strong is Mack and where is Vienna" the how-many pattern captures "Mack and where is Vienna", finds two names and returns None (`question_desk.py:116-149`, `:213-215`); the state desk then builds `enemy_at` with place = Vienna and prints "No, Sire — Mack stands at Swabia, not Vienna" (`state_desk.py:596-600`, `:2353-2357`); "where is Lannes and who holds Bohemia" fails the same way to the shrug. **Sightings:** conquest #1 (P3, turn 1, action 5, `docs/audits/dd_b/conquest/frames/0005.jpg`); conquest #8 (P3, turn 3, action 60, `docs/audits/dd_b/conquest/frames/0060.jpg`). **Decided fix:** A line joining two questions (" and " + where / who / how / what) is split and each part answered; `enemy_at` sets a place only when "at / in <place>" follows the foe. |
| **DDB-46** | P3 | FIXED October 19, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 4 (`94ce4c44`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_voice.py::TestDDB46`; the deficit and brewing cards end with their state; a one-shot event posts at HIGH and ages out after its turn (`notifications.EVENT_NOTICE_TYPES`, `retire_aged_events` at the advance); the siblings DDB-X30, X31; the sighting's re-play is DD-B's re-measure, S14e, which reads every road again); was: the decided fix below holds, `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_voice.py::TestDDB46` pins it, and S13b's closing re-play on the DD-B instrument shows the sighting gone ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=narration⟩ | **The notice rail keeps stale cards, and old events lead it forever.** State cards are never retired when the state ends: the deficit card on recovery (`world_state.py:8185-8189`), the brewing card when the coalition forms (`coalition.py:3328-3344`); one-shot event notices posted at CRITICAL ("orders lost", `combat_executor.py:5536-5543`; "Armistice Collapsed", `diplomacy.py:11047-11052`) are never evicted by the cap and sort first (`notifications.py:405-408`, `:440-444`; `notification_bar.gd:396-406`). **Sightings:** conquest #9 (P3, turn 4, action 74, `docs/audits/dd_b/conquest/frames/0074.jpg`); conquest #33 (P3, turn 19, action 354, `docs/audits/dd_b/conquest/frames/0354.jpg`); the sea #8 (P3, turn 3, action 64, `docs/audits/dd_b/sea/frames/0064.jpg`). **Decided fix:** A state card is dismissed when its state ends; an event notice posts at HIGH and ages out after its turn. |

| **DDB-48** | P3 | FIXED October 19, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 4 (`94ce4c44`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_voice.py::TestDDB48`; `backend/ai/help_topics.py` — a "how do / can I" question gets the reference's ONE section its nouns name, `help <topic>` one section; the reference gains PORTS AND THE CONTINENTAL SYSTEM, built from the Admiralty's constants; the sighting's re-play is DD-B's re-measure, S14e, which reads every road again); was: the decided fix below holds, `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_voice.py::TestDDB48` pins it, and S13b's closing re-play on the DD-B instrument shows the sighting gone ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=command⟩ | **"How do I …?" dumps the whole command reference instead of answering.** Any "how do / can I …" matches `_SYNTAX_QUESTION_RE` and is sent to the full manual on purpose (`llm_client.py:960-973`, `:3175-3182`; `meta_executor.py:864-883`); the manual has no section for ports, the Continental System, fleets' postures or readiness; "help" matches exact phrases only, so "help navy" falls to the generic "this order eludes me" (`llm_client.py:2440`, `:3473`). **Sightings:** diplomacy-first #8 (P3, turn 2, action 59, `docs/audits/dd_b/diplomacy/frames/0059.jpg`); diplomacy-first #21 (P3, turn 5, action 161, `docs/audits/dd_b/diplomacy/frames/0161.jpg`); the sea #1 (P3, turn 1, action 8, `docs/audits/dd_b/sea/frames/0008.jpg`); the sea #5 (P3, turn 1, action 26, `docs/audits/dd_b/sea/frames/0026.jpg`); the sea #9 (P3, turn 3, action 67, `docs/audits/dd_b/sea/frames/0067.jpg`); the sea #22 (P3, turn 12, action 308, `docs/audits/dd_b/sea/frames/0308.jpg`). **Decided fix:** A "how do / can I <verb> …" question is answered by the manual's ONE section its nouns name (fleet / blockade / readiness → the naval section; several marshals → the support and muster section), and "help <topic>" prints one section; the manual gains a naval-and-ports section. |

| **DDB-59** | P3 | FIXED October 19, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 4 (`94ce4c44`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_sea.py::TestDDB59`; `naval.pooled_sail_clause` in the crossings legend ("Spain's 30 sail already count"); the own fleet's `camp_line`; the sighting's re-play is DD-B's re-measure, S14e, which reads every road again); was: the decided fix below holds, `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_sea.py::TestDDB59` pins it, and S13b's closing re-play on the DD-B instrument shows the sighting gone ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=naval⟩ | **The Admiralty's "pooling a fleet" and "staging the camp" read as orders; both are automatic states.** Pooling is no order: an ally at war with the same foe adds 80% of her sail on her own (`naval.py:302-303`, `:429-462`), yet the legend says a crossing "opens by building or pooling a fleet" (`naval.py:3539-3542`, `:1669`); "staged" means two consecutive end-of-turn checks with 40,000 in the camp while at war with the island power, reset by any truce (`naval.py:2566-2600`, `:2235-2237`), and the ledger shows the men but never the count (`strategic_ledger.gd:917-924`). **Sightings:** the sea #4 (P3, turn 1, action 23, `docs/audits/dd_b/sea/frames/0023.jpg`); the sea #13 (P3, turn 5, action 104, `docs/audits/dd_b/sea/frames/0104.jpg`). **Decided fix:** The legend says an ally's sail already counts ("Spain's 30 sail already count"); the camp line reads "staged after 2 turns standing at war with Britain (1 of 2) — no order needed", and "no army is staged" says why. |

| **DDB-61** | P3 | FIXED October 19, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 4 (`94ce4c44`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_sea.py::TestDDB61`; `naval.window_remedy` on the rot (the keel receipt, the Admiralty's `rot_line`); the blockade chip's note states the price before the order; `naval.posture_phrase` — "ordered to blockade stations — Britain still pins her in port" — on the war banner, the order and the ledger; the sighting's re-play is DD-B's re-measure, S14e, which reads every road again); was: the decided fix below holds, `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_sea.py::TestDDB61` pins it, and S13b's closing re-play on the DD-B instrument shows the sighting gone ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=naval⟩ | **The Admiralty never says what stops the readiness rot, nor what a blockade order costs, before the order.** The keel receipt says the rot "is the number to fix" with no remedy (`naval_executor.py:83-98`); the remedy sentence exists but only in the Diversion forecast (`naval.py:2833-2851`, `_window_remedy`); the "Blockade the enemy" chip note lists only what it closes (`naval.py:3692-3714`), and the self-blockade rot and "our coasts go unguarded" are said only after the order is spent (`naval_executor.py:315-325`); a blockaded fleet may still take the blockade posture, so "pinned in port" and "stands out to sea" both print (`naval.py:3469`, `war_status.py:550`). **Sightings:** the sea #9 (P3, turn 3, action 67, `docs/audits/dd_b/sea/frames/0067.jpg`); the sea #10 (P3, turn 3, action 68, `docs/audits/dd_b/sea/frames/0068.jpg`). **Decided fix:** The rot line carries its remedy (`_window_remedy`); the chip note carries the self-blockade clause and the uncovered coast; a self-blockaded fleet's order reads "ordered to blockade stations — Britain still pins her". |

| **DDB-R1** | P2 | BUILT October 15, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 3 (`ab6314a9`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_rulings.py::TestDDBR1`; `combat_executor.pursuit_ask`: a typed attack out of reach asks at no cost, naming the price and the first march; the answer re-issues the attack confirmed through CR-2's grammar (option `flags`); `SYSTEMS_REFERENCE.md` §118.2; the sighting's re-play is S14e's); was: the conquest line "Ney, attack Kutuzov in Moravia" typed with Ney in Bohemia asks, spends nothing and names the pursuit's price and first march; yes pursues with NPC-D4's terms, no spends nothing; the AI's and the strategic roads are unchanged; BASELINE_SERIES and M1–M7 byte-identical; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_rulings.py::TestDDBR1` pins it ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=command⟩ | **Build `DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md` DDB-D1's ruling — An attack on a marshal out of reach silently becomes a 2-AP pursuit that marches at once.** **Ruling:** ASK FIRST. An attack on a marshal out of reach asks, at no cost: "Kutuzov stands at Moravia, two marches off. Pursue him (2 AP — a standing order; the first march takes him to Dresden, Saxony's soil), or cancel?" — yes reissues the pursuit with NPC-D4's terms; typed yes / pursue / no / cancel answer it (CR-2's grammar). Typed player orders only: the post-objection road, `take <foe>` and strategic execution keep today's upgrade; the AI never reaches it. The literal marshal's ask of the same shape is the precedent (`combat_executor.py:6530-6572`). Supersedes NPC-D4's disclose-only answer (a delegate ruling, October 2); no ruling of the user's is reversed. **Sightings:** conquest #13 (P2, turn 5, action 98, `docs/audits/dd_b/conquest/frames/0098.jpg`). |
| **DDB-R2** | P2 | BUILT October 15, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 3 (`ab6314a9`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_rulings.py::TestDDBR2`; `combat_executor.player_muster_gate_arms`: an unfavourable band pauses any player lead (the sovereign never), Berthier naming it for a non-cautious one; the commit skips the second objection draw; `what_if_line` rides every muster on a result; the help and the School's card teach the preview; §118.3; the sighting's re-play is S14e's); was: an unfavourable attack by a non-cautious marshal pauses on the muster with Commit / Cancel (Cancel 0 AP), Berthier naming the band; a favourable attack fires at once; the sovereign never pauses; a committed attack draws its objection once; every muster riding a result ends with the what-if line, and the help and the tutor's card name it; the AI's gate constants unchanged and BASELINE_SERIES byte-identical; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_rulings.py::TestDDBR2` pins it ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=combat_legibility⟩ | **Build `DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md` DDB-D2's ruling — The muster arrives with the battle's result: a report, not a preview.** **Ruling:** WIDEN THE GATE TO "POTENTIAL DISASTER" AND TEACH THE FREE PREVIEW. Re-opens the user's own CA9-D2 (August 9: "only show popup if they are entering potential disaster and general is cautious") on its own stated condition — its record left "the feel question" to a playtest, and DD-B's showed three non-cautious leads walking into unfavourable odds unwarned. (1) The muster gate arms on an UNFAVOURABLE band for ANY personality (the disaster test kept, the cautious clause dropped); a favourable attack still fires at once (CR-6 (b)/(d) kept); the sovereign keeps NO CONFIRM (§15.9a). A NEW player-only predicate at the gate site — `MUSTER_GATE_BAND` / `MUSTER_GATE_PERSONALITIES` untouched, so the AI's gate and every series hold; Berthier, not the marshal, names the band for a non-cautious lead; the commit's re-issue is exempt from a second objection draw (`executor.py:2284-2296`). (2) Every muster that rides a result ends "Ask 'what if Ney attacks Mack' to read the muster before you commit — it costs nothing"; the help's battle section and the tutor's muster card name it. Not taken: an always-preview setting; arming on a favourable-but-incomplete muster (about half of all attacks would pause). **Sightings:** conquest #15 (P2, turn 6, action 112, `docs/audits/dd_b/conquest/frames/0112.jpg`); diplomacy-first #9 (P2, turn 2, action 64, `docs/audits/dd_b/diplomacy/frames/0064.jpg`); diplomacy-first #13 (P3, turn 3, action 91, `docs/audits/dd_b/diplomacy/frames/0091.jpg`); the sea #2 (P3, turn 1, action 12, `docs/audits/dd_b/sea/frames/0012.jpg`); the sea #7 (P2, turn 1, action 28, `docs/audits/dd_b/sea/frames/0028.jpg`); the sea #14 (P2, turn 5, action 109, `docs/audits/dd_b/sea/frames/0109.jpg`). |
| **DDB-R3** | P2 | BUILT October 15, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 3 (`89db8acc`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_rulings.py::TestDDBR3`; `garrison_report.detachment_capitulates` read by `garrison_exchange` (both boards, the desk's forecast); every collapse exit emits `garrison_destroyed`; BASELINE_SERIES byte-identical on its arm (N — no detachment capitulates in the ambient sim; the series re-pin is DDB-X3's); the sf_page CMD-H-DOWN arm holds it down with the driver's new `--seam` (Archduke Charles takes Franconia whole at turn 34); §118.7; the sighting's re-play is S14e's); was: a 3,000 detachment assaulted at ≥ 4:1 effective odds falls in one assault, its garrison event emitted; at 2:1 it loses the capped half; a capital at 5:1 and a depot keep the 0.50 cap; both boards one arithmetic; BASELINE_SERIES re-pinned with this row named and its attribution arm recorded; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_rulings.py::TestDDBR3` pins it ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=combat_legibility⟩ | **Build `DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md` DDB-D3's ruling — Each assault on a garrison only halves it, whatever the odds.** **Ruling:** BUILD FA-D28'S OPEN HALF FOR DETACHMENTS. At ≥ 4:1 effective odds an assault takes a detachment whole (it capitulates — Memmingen and Ulm, October 1805); below 4:1 today's capped exchange stands; a capital's own garrison and a DEF-6 depot keep the 0.50 cap (FA-D28's own fix shape, September 4). | **DDB-R4** | P3 | BUILT October 15, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 3 (`ab6314a9`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_rulings.py::TestDDBR4`; the end-turn mirror, WO-22's defer, C3's guard, the `should_end_turn` keys and the client's AUTO_END copy retired; the last order of either pool says so; `auto_advanced_to_turn` stays readable; §118.4; the sighting's re-play is S14e's); was: spending the last military action leaves the turn unchanged with "the last order of the day"; "end turn" then advances, guarded by the client's envoy and last-stand gate; the mirror, WO-22's defer, the unread keys and the AUTO_END_WARNING copy are gone; old saves load; BASELINE_SERIES and M1–M7 byte-identical; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_rulings.py::TestDDBR4` pins it ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=command⟩ | **Build `DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md` DDB-D4's ruling — The last action of the day ends the turn by itself.** **Ruling:** NO AUTO-END ON EITHER POOL. Spending the last action no longer ends the turn: the receipt carries AAR-12's "the last order of the day", the End Turn button turns gold, the player ends the turn. §6 row 21(b)'s pre-stated re-open condition is met (conquest #27: a turn ended by surprise despite the warning line); its remedy, a confirm on the last order, is not taken — a modal on the commonest click taxes every turn, while no-auto-end costs one press on a fully spent turn. Retired with it: the ~245-line end-turn mirror (`executor.py:3639-3884`), WO-22's defer and its missed last-stand case (the client's one gate then guards every end turn), the unread `should_end_turn` keys (`diplomatic_executor.py:5528-5536`, `economy_executor.py:1969-1970`), the AUTO_END_WARNING copy. The save's `auto_advanced_to_turn` stays readable. Re-opens AAR-12's scope and row 21(b) (both delegate rulings). **Sightings:** conquest #27 (P3, turn 17, action 314, `docs/audits/dd_b/conquest/frames/0314.jpg`). |
| **DDB-R5** | P3 | BUILT October 15, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 3 (`ab6314a9`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_rulings.py::TestDDBR5`; `economy_executor.named_arm_refusal`: refused before anything is spent, naming both roads; pre-validated; PF-7's pins flipped with this row named; §118.5; the sighting's re-play is S14e's); was: "recruit artillery for Augereau" spends nothing (gold, the admin action, the pool unchanged) and names both roads; PF-7's pin flipped with this row named; no AI path changes; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_rulings.py::TestDDBR5` pins it ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=economy⟩ | **Build `DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md` DDB-D5's ruling — A named marshal's arm replaces the arm the player asked to recruit, after the gold is spent.** **Ruling:** REFUSE AT NO COST, NAMING BOTH ROADS (CN-2's own pre-stated branch). | **DDB-R6** | P3 | BUILT October 15, 2026 — Pre-Deploy S13b part 3 (`89db8acc`; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_rulings.py::TestDDBR6`; the engaged move's refusal builds its friendly list with `retreat_soil_is_friendly`, says "withdraw" and names "'Davout, retreat to Swabia' (free, −45% effectiveness, once a turn)" (`movement_executor.retreat_price_phrase`); §118.8; the sighting's re-play is S14e's); was: diplomacy #16's line ("Davout, move to Swabia" while engaged, Swabia allied) refuses and names "Davout, retreat to Swabia" with its price; the refusal reads `retreat_soil_is_friendly`; no series moves; `tests/test_ddb_s13b_the_rulings.py::TestDDBR6` pins it ⟨SF step=pre-deploy S13 · DD-B · pillar=command⟩ | **Build `DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md` DDB-D6's ruling — An engaged marshal cannot fall back onto an ally's province, and the refusal says "Cannot advance".** **Ruling:** KEEP THE RULE, FIX THE SENTENCE. Engaged means fight, stand or retreat: a free disengage by `move` would undercut the retreat's price and the AI's engagement rung. But `retreat` already falls back onto an ally's or a vassal's province (AAR-D4), so the refusal's "he must fight or stand" is false there: it builds its friendly list with `retreat_soil_is_friendly`, says "withdraw" and names the order and its price ("'Davout, retreat to Swabia' — free, −X% effectiveness, once a turn"). The exploration found that edge case — and its neighbours — already live on the client; the plan (`~/.claude/plans/sorted-yawning-clover.md`, approved October 15, 2026) filed them here before any feature was built. ## UXR-3 — the review (October 13, 2026; Pre-Deploy S11; 84 rows: UXR3-1 … UXR3-73 for every ✗ and UXR3-F1 … F11 found while reading; S12 part 1's re-read closed 45 of the 73, part 2's closing re-read 24 more and F1 … F10; 4 re-homed to UXR-4 at S15 with their frames and the readers' reasons; F11 is S14's; each row says which)

> The look-and-feel review: 145 surfaces × the eight items of `docs/UX_CHECKLIST_V1.json` (frozen at `603d983f` before the first reading), read on that tree by the instruments and three blind readers. Review `docs/audits/UXR3_REVIEW_2026_10_13.md`; records `docs/audits/uxr3/`; rules `SYSTEMS_REFERENCE.md` §113; pins `tests/test_uxr3_checklist_frozen.py`, `tests/test_uxr3_the_review.py`.

**How these rows were filed** (the checklist's own filing rule):
- **Every ✗ is a row's surface and item.** 373 ✗ across 138 surfaces, in 73 rows. The ✗s of one item with one cause on several surfaces of one scene share a row, which names every surface and its frame. A surface the capture harness has never shot gets one row for all of its items, with the missing shot as its first fix.
- **The owner is S12, "UXR-3 fixes".** A row's completion is its item re-read ✓ on each named surface, against the same frozen checklist and the same tools.
- **Severity.** P2 for a player-visible item (R1, R2, R3, R5, R7, R8) on a surface of the top five groups. P3 otherwise, and for R4 (a source census) and R6 (a missing driven proof) everywhere. No crash and no SCRIPT ERROR was found, so there is no P1.
- **The spread.** A reader item carries its spread (3–0 or 2–1); a 2–1 ✗ is filed like a 3–0 ✗.
- **Found while reading (F1 … F11).** These are the readers' R4 notes and the conductor's checks: defects no item's mark rests on, each verified on its frame or carried by notes from two or three readers. F11 is a backend COPY row; the plan routes it to the ending pillar's owner (S14), never to UXR.
- **Already owned, cross-referenced and not re-filed:** UXR-X9 (the diorama's verdict can reach the nameplate) and UXR-X28 (the map's furniture crowds Central Europe). Both are in §UXR-2 above; X9 was fixed at S12 part 2, X28 at S12b's head (October 14, 2026).
- **The frames** are under `docs/audits/uxr3/frames/`: each surface's own panel, cropped from the 1920×1080 frame unless the row names another resolution, never scaled.
